The air in the meadow was thick with the scent of pine, warm earth, and sun-warmed hay. At dawn, the first light spilled over the hills like spilled honey, gilding the edge of the open field where the *Evergreen Festival* had begun. Thousands of people had gathered—some in borrowed clothes, others in hand-sewn dresses, in vintage bandanas and neon boots. A soft hum of anticipation rose like a tide, punctuated by the distant chime of a wind-up bell and the rustle of denim flapping in the breeze.
